Code quality review for Task 2 changes (commit `23674cd`).

## Working directory
`C:\Users\redna\.claude\.claude\worktrees\thirsty-roentgen-fc40ad`

## What changed

Four files were updated to migrate IVDR journey from `/` + `/station/:id` paths to `/ivdr` + `/ivdr/station/:id`:
- `ivdr-wiki/src/components/JourneyMap.tsx`
- `ivdr-wiki/src/components/DocumentWorkspace.tsx`
- `ivdr-wiki/src/components/ConceptPage.tsx`
- `ivdr-wiki/src/components/DocumentTree.tsx`

## Review focus

Check only the CHANGED portions:
1. Are the new Link elements consistent with the existing design patterns in each file (same classNames, same style props)?
2. Is the "← 인증 허브" link in JourneyMap accessible? (aria attributes if needed)
3. Is the "인증 허브" breadcrumb in DocumentWorkspace styled consistently with the other breadcrumbs?
4. Any `useCallback` dependencies affected by the path change? (`openStation` / `closeStation` deps should still be `[navigate]`)

Do NOT flag missing tests (no test framework in this project).

End with:
- `QUALITY_REVIEW: ✅ APPROVED`
- `QUALITY_REVIEW: ⚠️ ISSUES [list]`

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

content.text:
I now have a complete picture of all changes. Here is the review:

---

**1. New Link elements — consistency with existing design patterns**

**JourneyMap.tsx — "← 인증 허브" button (lines 127–132)**

The new Link is placed alongside two existing buttons in the same `flex flex-wrap gap-3` row. Comparing the three:

| Link | className | borderColor | color prop | minHeight |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 써야 할 문서 (existing) | `inline-flex items-center gap-2 rounded-[var(--r-md)] font-bold text-text-on-color` | — (filled) | `background: var(--accent)` | 44 |
| 개념 위키 (existing) | `inline-flex items-center gap-2 rounded-[var(--r-md)] border font-bold text-text hover:bg-surface` | `var(--border-strong)` | — | 44 |
| **← 인증 허브 (new)** | `inline-flex items-center gap-2 rounded-[var(--r-md)] border font-bold text-text-muted hover:bg-surface` | `var(--border)` | — | 44 |

The new button intentionally uses `text-text-muted` + `var(--border)` (weaker) to signal lower visual priority than "개념 위키" — this is a reasonable hierarchy choice. The `minHeight: 44`, `padding: "11px 18px"`, and font weight all match the existing pattern. Consistent.

**DocumentWorkspace.tsx — "인증 허브" breadcrumb (lines 72–78)**

The new "인증 허브" breadcrumb is the first item in the breadcrumb row. Comparing it to all siblings:

- `인증 허브` (new): `className="inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-[var(--r-full)] font-semibold text-text-muted hover:text-text"`, style `{ fontSize: "var(--t-xs)", border: "1px solid var(--border)", padding: "3px 10px" }` — **no icon**
- `IVDR 여정` (new): same className + style, has `<Compass size={13} aria-hidden />`
- `문서 목록` (existing): identical className + style, has `<FileText size={13} aria-hidden />`
- `정거장 N · Phase` (existing, accent-colored link): different styling (no pill, no border), colored by phase

The "인증 허브" breadcrumb is consistent with "IVDR 여정" and "문서 목록" in className and style. Intentionally has no icon (it's the root hub, no icon is fine). Styling is fully consistent.

**ConceptPage.tsx and DocumentTree.tsx — station link path update**

Both are pure path string changes (`/station/` → `/ivdr/station/`). No className, style, or structure changed. Consistent.

---

**2. "← 인증 허브" accessibility (JourneyMap)**

The link at line 127 renders visible text `← 인증 허브`. The destination is `/` (the certification hub home).

- The arrow character `←` is a Unicode character in text content — screen readers will announce it as "left arrow 인증 허브" in Korean TTS, which is acceptable but mildly verbose. A cleaner approach would be `aria-label="인증 허브로 돌아가기"` to suppress the arrow from the accessible name, but this is the same pattern used by ConceptPage's `← 개념 목록` link (line 39 of ConceptPage.tsx) and is consistent with that established pattern. No structural aria issue.
- `minHeight: 44` ensures 44 px touch target — meets WCAG 2.5.5.
- No additional aria attributes are needed given the consistent pattern used across the codebase.

**Minor note:** The link lacks `aria-label`, but this matches the `← 개념 목록` pattern already in ConceptPage. Not a new issue introduced by this commit.

---

**3. "인증 허브" breadcrumb styling consistency (DocumentWorkspace)**

Reviewed above in point 1. The new crumb matches `IVDR 여정` and `문서 목록` exactly in className and style. The breadcrumb row has no `<nav aria-label>` wrapper, but that was pre-existing — not introduced here. No issue with the changed code.

---

**4. `useCallback` dependencies (JourneyMap)**

```ts
const openStation = useCallback(
  (sid: number) => navigate(`/ivdr/station/${sid}`),
  [navigate],                        // ✅ correct
);
const closeStation = useCallback(() => navigate("/ivdr"), [navigate]); // ✅ correct
```

The path strings `/ivdr/station/${sid}` and `/ivdr` are literals, not variables — they introduce no new dependencies. Both callbacks correctly list only `[navigate]`. No issue.

---

**Summary**

All four changes are:
- Internally consistent with existing className/style patterns
- Correctly scoped `useCallback` deps
- Accessible at the same level as the rest of the codebase

`QUALITY_REVIEW: ✅ APPROVED`
